summary: Bay Minette and Gulf Shores police each arrested a man Sunday on methamphetamine-possession charges, the jail roster shows; the roster listed no new admissions in the 24 hours before about 4:45 a.m. Monday. The man the sheriff's office booked Saturday on child sex-abuse charges remained in custody.

entries.agency: Bay Minette Police; Gulf Shores Police
entries.title: Methamphetamine arrests, Bay Minette and Gulf Shores: Shawn Michael Sutherland, Early Lee Lymon
body: Bay Minette police arrested Shawn Michael Sutherland, 28, at 8:46 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, and Gulf Shores police arrested Early Lee Lymon, 44, at 8:44 a.m. the same day, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found for either arrest.

Sutherland was booked on charges of methamphetamine possession and possession of drug paraphernalia. Lymon was booked on charges of methamphetamine possession, possession of drug paraphernalia and second-degree marijuana possession — possession for personal use. Both were in custody when the roster was read early Monday.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 22: Carlos Barrera, Jaterah Arianna Simon, Randall Jack Morris and others
body: The sheriff's office arrested Carlos Barrera, 52, at 4:38 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, on charges of possession of dangerous drugs and drug paraphernalia, and Randall Jack Morris, 68, at 4:01 p.m. on a felony failure-to-appear warrant; both were in custody early Monday. Deputies also arrested Zechariah Troy Dale Scott, 30, Sunday morning on a methamphetamine-possession charge; the roster shows him released the same day.

Bay Minette police arrested Jaterah Arianna Simon, 26, at 4:15 p.m. Sunday on a theft charge, and Kristi Campbell Smith, 53, Sunday night on two failure-to-appear warrants. Fairhope police arrested Brian Christopher Lee Russell, 29, at 10:12 a.m. Sunday; the roster lists possession of dangerous drugs and second-degree marijuana possession, and Fairhope's arrest log lists unlawful possession of a controlled substance, psilocin — the active compound in psychedelic mushrooms. He was released the same day. Kedrick Dewain Parker, 45, arrested by Bay Minette police early Sunday on a drunk-driving charge, was released Nov. 22. All information is from the jail roster and the Fairhope police log.

entries.title: Child sex-abuse arrest: Christopher Paul Phillips
body: Christopher Paul Phillips, 34, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 9:15 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.

He was booked on charges of sexual abuse of a child under 12 — sexual contact with a young child — first-degree sodomy — a forcible or non-consensual sexual act — and child abuse. He was in custody when the roster was read early Monday.

entries.title: Methamphetamine and coercion arrest, Loxley: Brady Kristopher Mashburn
body: Brady Kristopher Mashburn, 28, was arrested by Loxley police at 7:23 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the jail roster.

He was booked on charges of methamphetamine possession and coercion, which the roster lists as harassment or intimidation — using threats to make someone act. He was in custody when the roster was read early Monday.

entries.title: Impersonating a police officer arrest, Spanish Fort: Thomas Earl Sawyer
body: Thomas Earl Sawyer, 76, was arrested by Spanish Fort police at 2 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found.
He was booked on a charge of impersonating a peace officer — falsely claiming to be a police officer. The roster shows him released Nov. 21.

entries.title: Protection-order violation arrest, Gulf Shores: Leslie Daniel Hurst
body: Leslie Daniel Hurst, 43, was arrested by Gulf Shores police at 7:38 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, and booked into the county jail Saturday, according to the jail roster.
He was booked on a charge of violating a domestic violence protection order — breaking a court order to stay away from someone. The roster shows him released Nov. 22.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 20–21: Jason Allen Cochran, Kenzie Rose Dumond, Danielle Lashay Leanna Carley and others
body: The sheriff's office booked Jason Allen Cochran, 53, Saturday night, Nov. 21, on a felony failure-to-appear warrant and other failure-to-appear warrants, and Chester Louis Davis II, 55, on a harassment charge; the roster shows Davis released Nov. 22. Deputies booked Kenzie Rose Dumond, 30, Saturday morning on a harassment charge involving a family member.
Gulf Shores police arrested Danielle Lashay Leanna Carley, 27, as a fugitive from justice Friday night, Nov. 20. All information is from the jail roster.

entries.title: Child abuse arrest, Fairhope daycare teacher: Abigail Leigh Bourgeois
body: Abigail Leigh Bourgeois, 22, who worked as a teacher at a Fairhope daycare, is accused in a criminal complaint filed in Baldwin County District Court of grabbing a child in her care by the arm and dragging the child across the floor on Sept. 22, FOX10 reported Friday. The complaint lists one felony count of child abuse, according to the station. The daycare told FOX10 it reported the matter to authorities.

She was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 10 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, and booked on a charge the roster lists as torture or willful abuse of a child, non-family — abuse of a child outside the household. The roster shows her released Nov. 20. A complaint is an accusation, not a finding of guilt.

entries.title: Federal indictment, threats against first responders: Gorden Ellis Wade
body: A federal grand jury has indicted Gorden Ellis Wade of Elberta on one count of transmitting a threatening communication in interstate commerce, FOX10 reported Friday. The indictment, filed Nov. 18 in U.S. District Court in Mobile, alleges that on or about Nov. 6 he posted on Facebook a threat to injure first responders in Alabama, according to the station.

Wade also faces a state charge in Baldwin County of making a terrorist threat in the first degree. He was released from the county jail Nov. 7 on a $7,500 bond and arrested Nov. 12 on the federal charge; he is held in the Escambia County, Alabama, jail, FOX10 reported. The federal count carries a maximum of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, according to a penalty sheet cited by the station. Arraignment is set for Dec. 2. An indictment is an accusation, not a finding of guilt.
